Ana (Product): Ok team - need to lock Q3 perf initiatives today. Customer pilot (AcmePayments) is asking for much tighter SLAs. Thinking focus areas: kernels (fusion), quantization workstream, and KV cache ops.

Jamal (Eng Runtime): Agree. Can we break kernels into 2-week spikes: 1) MHA fusion + kernel autotune, 2) rollout + perf regressions. Quant can be parallel but QA heavy.

Katie (ML): For quant, we need a clear quality SLA. Proposal: no more than 1% drop in end-to-end metric on our chat eval set (turn-level ROUGE/embedding-sim). If exceeded -> hold rollout.

Leo (Infra): If we enable fused kernels + int8 paths we'll need an additional kernel fallback layer for older GPUs. Ops cost impact estimate coming but expect some node churn.

Sarah (SRE): Rollout plan must include automated canary and auto-fallback. Canary size: 1% traffic, watch p95, error rate, and payload diffs. If p95 regresses by >10% or error rate +0.1% then rollback.

Ana (Product): Customers: AcmePayments target is p95 < 40ms for 256 token baseline (they measured on our hosted API). That's strict. Can we set internal OKR that balances latency and accuracy?

Jamal (Eng Runtime): Suggest OKRs: ["Reduce p95 decode latency by 30% for 256/512 token profiles on standard A100 configs","Reduce per-token cost by 15% via quant + kernel improvements","KV cache hit rate >= 70% for typical multi-turn chat workloads"]. Those are ambitious but measurable.

Katie (ML): +1 but add a quality guard: "Regression on eval harness <= 1% for production prompts". We need automated eval gating in CI.

Leo (Infra): Realistic timeline: kernels proto (2 sprints), quant proto (3 sprints including eval), KV cache improvements (1 sprint infra + 2 sprints runtime). We can overlap but not fully parallel.

Sarah (SRE): Launch criteria checklist draft: 
```
- Latency target met for canary (p95 within target)
- Quality gate passed on eval harness
- No more than 0.1% error increase vs baseline
- Rollout automation + rollback verified
- Runbook updated, oncall aware
```

Jamal (Eng Runtime): Tradeoffs to call out: prioritizing quantization will drive biggest cost wins but increases QA work and slows kernel refactor. If AcmePayments is blocking, consider a two-track: quick kernel tuning + KV cache to hit latency, follow-up quant in Q3+1.

Ana (Product): That two-track approach seems pragmatic. We should be explicit about customer-facing commit vs internal optimizations. Acme wants a date — propose an early canary in 7 weeks and GA in 12 if no blockers.

Katie (ML): We need to agree on measurement: define canonical load profile and synthetic trace for 256/512 tokens, plus a small slice of production traffic for A/B. I'll upload eval sets.

Jamal (Eng Runtime): Action items: 
- Jamal: scope kernel spike + perf benchmarks (due in 5d)
- Katie: upload eval harness + quality thresholds (due in 3d)
- Leo: infra cost + fallback plan (due in 7d)
- Sarah: canary + rollback playbook draft (due in 7d)
- Ana: commit customer communication + proposed dates (due EOD)

perf-bot: perf alert template created for canary: p95_latency, error_rate, model_output_drift.

Ana (Product): OK, if everyone hits those dates we'll present to PM leadership on Friday. Thanks. :thumbsup:

Jamal (Eng Runtime): Noted. Will post a brief RFC for kernel changes with perf numbers once spike completes.

Katie (ML): I'll run adversarial prompts through quantized models and report deltas.

Leo (Infra): Starting capacity planning now. Will flag any region constraints.

Sarah (SRE): I'll sync with oncall and schedule a dry-run of rollback next week.

Ana (Product): Great. Closing thread — will follow up with the draft customer note after EOD.
